interest: Shows a Connecticut businessman using Senator Copeland to seek Japan's postal life insurance report via State.
overview: This file (894.5064/14) concerns an inquiry initiated by Charles W. Palomba of Waterbury, Connecticut, and forwarded to the Department of State by Senator Royal S. Copeland, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Commerce, requesting a copy of an official English-language report published by the Japanese Government on the Japanese Post Office Insurance System. Palomba's interest had been stimulated by an article in the January 18, 1934 issue of 'The Spectator' (An American Weekly Review of Insurance). Secretary of State Cordell Hull responded that the American Consul General at Tokyo had previously sent a copy of this report to the Department on February 27, 1935, which had been transferred to the Department of Labor. Hull transmitted a copy of the Consul General's accompanying despatch outlining the salient features of the report and advised that Palomba could either seek a loan of the publication from the Department of Labor or authorize the State Department to instruct the Consul General at Tokyo to purchase an additional copy on his behalf.
